open_points.subject: All validation functions
open_points.text: “raises RefusedError naming the first failing check” and “MUST raise UnknownReferenceError naming…”; no constructor signatures or required message/reason format are supplied for RefusedError or UnknownReferenceError
open_points.question: How must each exception be instantiated, and what exact value or text constitutes ‘naming’ a reference, port, check, field, ceiling, or reason?
options: Pass a single formatted string
Pass the referenced identifier/reason as a positional value
Use keyword fields defined outside this prompt
open_points.default_guess: Pass one descriptive string containing every item the note requires to be named.

open_points.subject: Enum use throughout the module
open_points.text: “Python member names were not available in models context” is stated for every imported enum
open_points.question: Should enum values be constructed by calling the enum class with its serialized string, or are particular Python member names expected?
options: Call each enum class with the listed serialized value
Use inferred uppercase member names
Pass serialized strings directly to model constructors
open_points.default_guess: Construct enums by calling the enum class with the listed serialized value.

open_points.subject: Byte digest creation
open_points.text: “value_digest is content_identity of the bytes” conflicts with “def content_identity(subject: IdentitySubject) -> str”
open_points.question: Which IdentitySubject must wrap raw bytes before content_identity is called?
options: BytesContent(subject_kind='bytes', content=bytes)
Pass bytes directly despite the declared signature
Use another unspecified canonical content model
open_points.default_guess: Wrap the bytes in BytesContent.

open_points.subject: Stored schema for many ports
open_points.text: “for a many port the canonical array schema with it as items”
open_points.question: What exact JSON string, including parsing and serialization rules, represents the canonical array schema used in StoredValue.value_schema and therefore in value_id?
options: Parse the port schema and serialize {'type':'array','items':schema} with sorted compact JSON
Embed the original schema text as the items value
Use a predefined canonical schema helper not imported here
open_points.default_guess: Parse the schema and compactly serialize an object with type 'array' and the parsed schema as items, using sorted keys.

open_points.subject: Kernel actor
open_points.text: “admit_implementation: MUST act as the kernel actor” while Actor also requires agent_name: str | None
open_points.question: What agent_name must the kernel Actor carry?
options: None
A fixed string such as 'kernel'
The submitting actor's agent_name
open_points.default_guess: Use Actor(kind=ActorKind('kernel'), agent_name=None).

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case
open_points.text: “MUST first read the Implementation … then raises RefusedError … that implementation's contract_version_id differs …; then each input port…”
open_points.question: When and how is named_contract_version_id resolved, and does an unknown named contract version raise UnknownReferenceError before or after the implementation-version mismatch check?
options: Compare the implementation's stored ID first, then read the named contract version
Read both records before comparing
Use the implementation's contract version after equality without separately resolving the named ID
open_points.default_guess: Read the implementation, compare its contract_version_id to the supplied ID, then read that contract version.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case inputs
open_points.text: “each input port in port name order does not fit … values read from their StoredValues … each spooled file of a SpooledFilesRef…”
open_points.question: Which PortRef variants are legal, and how are unknown names, duplicate names, missing ports, FileFactsRef inputs, cardinality mismatches, or multiple refs for one port handled and ordered?
options: Require exactly every contract input and allow only StoredValuesRef or SpooledFilesRef in the expected representation
Allow any subset and validate only supplied refs
Delegate all structural handling to fit_port_value
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one logical payload per contract input, reject unknown, duplicate, missing, and unsupported ref shapes before fit checks.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case source
open_points.text: “origin captured and captured_from the given source”
open_points.question: Must every SpooledFileKey belong to the supplied AttemptKey, and must the executed implementation be shown to have executed that attempt?
options: Validate both relationships
Validate only spool keys against source
Treat source as metadata only
open_points.default_guess: Treat source as metadata only because no relationship check is specified.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case referenced records
open_points.text: “values read from their StoredValues” and “each spooled file … taken by its SpooledFile facts”
open_points.question: What happens when a StoredValuesRef value_id or SpooledFileKey does not resolve, and in what order are such missing references checked?
options: Raise UnknownReferenceError in port/file order
Raise RefusedError as a fit failure
Assume referential integrity and index the query result
open_points.default_guess: Raise UnknownReferenceError for the first unresolved reference in port order and file-list order.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case copied files
open_points.text: “files becoming file-carriage StoredValues for the copied digests”
open_points.question: What exact media_type, size_bytes, value_schema, and value_id inputs are used for each copied file, especially if port metadata and SpooledFile facts disagree beyond the explicitly checked media type and size ceiling?
options: Use the port schema/media type and SpooledFile digest/size
Use all SpooledFile facts except disclosure class
Use facts returned by put_value_bytes
open_points.default_guess: Use the port's stored schema and media type, the SpooledFile digest and size, and derive value_id from StoredValueContent.

open_points.subject: add_captured_trial_case equal case
open_points.text: “Only after every check passed, each spooled file's bytes are read … and published” and “the equal existing one unchanged … otherwise the one written”
open_points.question: Must equality be checked before copying file bytes so that an equal existing case performs no byte publication, or are files copied before discovering the existing case?
options: Compute refs and trial_case_id, check existence, then copy only for a new case
Copy after validation and then check case existence
Republish bytes even when the case exists
open_points.default_guess: Check for the existing trial_case_id before reading or publishing spooled bytes.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case payloads
open_points.text: “each input port … by fit_port_value … a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size and the port's media type”
open_points.question: Which PortPayload variants are accepted for each carriage/cardinality combination, and how is a wrong payload variant converted into a candidate so fit_port_value can report carriage rather than failing during field access?
options: Map JsonPayload, FilePayload, and FileListPayload to their corresponding candidate types regardless of the declared port
Reject wrong payload classes directly
Construct a null candidate for any mismatched payload type
open_points.default_guess: Map each declared payload variant to JsonCandidate, FileCandidate, or FileListCandidate and let fit_port_value decide carriage.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case file candidates
open_points.text: “a file candidate taking the payload's digest, size” conflicts with FilePayload having only “port” and “content”, and FileListPayload having only “port” and “contents”
open_points.question: How are the digest and size used in FileFacts derived from file payload bytes?
options: Digest BytesContent via content_identity and use len(content)
Use put_value_bytes to obtain the digest before validation
Use an unspecified raw-byte digest function
open_points.default_guess: Use content_identity(BytesContent(...)) and len(content), without writing bytes during validation.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case persistence
open_points.text: “an existing equal case is returned with its first place and nothing is written” and “the bytes are stored with put_value_bytes”
open_points.question: Are put_value_bytes calls prohibited for an equal existing case, and therefore must all StoredValue identities and the TrialCaseContent be computed before storing any bytes?
options: Do not call put_value_bytes for an existing case
Allow idempotent put_value_bytes calls but no record_change
Always store bytes before checking case identity
open_points.default_guess: Do not call put_value_bytes when the case already exists.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case disclosure class
open_points.text: “each expected output … [uses] the highest class of the case's inputs from highest_disclosure_class”
open_points.question: What disclosure class is used when a contract has no input ports and expected outputs are supplied?
options: A fixed lowest class such as open
Reject contracts or cases with no inputs
Call highest_disclosure_class with an empty tuple and rely on its behavior
open_points.default_guess: Call highest_disclosure_class with the empty tuple because no fallback class is specified.

open_points.subject: add_trial_case return position
open_points.text: “corpus_position, its zero-based index in corpus order”
open_points.question: After insertion, should corpus_position be obtained from the returned RecordSet, by rereading the corpus, or inferred from the prior corpus length, particularly under concurrent writes?
options: Reread the corpus and locate trial_case_id
Use the inserted TrialCase.store_position even though TrialCase has no such field
Use the pre-insert corpus length
open_points.default_guess: Reread the corpus and locate the case by trial_case_id.

open_points.subject: admit_implementation reused verdict
open_points.text: “when a verdict over the current corpus digest exists for the implementation it is reused”
open_points.question: If the query returns more than one matching verdict, which one is reused?
options: Latest in store order
Earliest in store order
Treat multiple verdicts as impossible
open_points.default_guess: Use the latest matching verdict in store order.

open_points.subject: admit_implementation activation
open_points.text: “An admitted verdict activates the implementation … unless it already is … current activation” conflicts with “a new verdict sets activate true in its change”
open_points.question: When a new admitted verdict is recorded for an implementation that is already current, must RecordAdmissionVerdictChange.activate be true or false, and may that create another Activation?
options: Set activate false because it is already current
Set activate true as explicitly stated for every new verdict
Set activate true but require the store not to append a duplicate activation
open_points.default_guess: Set activate true as the more specific field-assignment instruction, relying on store semantics for the resulting activation.

open_points.subject: admit_implementation timestamps
open_points.text: A new verdict has “decided_at” and may activate “in the same request,” but no rule says whether timestamp calls are shared
open_points.question: Should verdict decision and activation use one KernelInstant or separate kernel_now calls when activation is produced by the verdict change or by RecordActivationChange?
options: Use one instant for the encompassing change
Call kernel_now separately for each change
Let record_change supply activation time
open_points.default_guess: Use one kernel_now result per constructed change.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case input reconstruction
open_points.text: “read the case's input bytes … build one PortPayload per input port, a FileListPayload in list order for a many file port”
open_points.question: How are multiple PortRef objects grouped, which ref variants are legal for authored versus captured cases, and what happens for missing, duplicate, or malformed refs?
options: Group consecutive refs by port and support StoredValuesRef plus applicable file refs
Locate refs by name regardless of order and ignore extras
Assume every stored case is structurally valid
open_points.default_guess: Assume stored cases are valid, group refs by contract port name, and support the ref shapes emitted by both add functions.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case expected outputs
open_points.text: “every output's digest equals the expected one”
open_points.question: How are sandbox outputs matched to expected outputs when output tuples are reordered, missing, duplicated, extra, or have the wrong payload variant?
options: Match by port name and treat every structural difference as output_mismatch
Compare tuple positions only
Treat malformed succeeded output as contract_violation
open_points.default_guess: Match by contract port name; treat missing, extra, duplicate, wrong-carriage, or wrong-cardinality outputs as contract_violation.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case outcome precedence
open_points.text: “output_mismatch otherwise” and “a succeeded value output whose canonical bytes exceed … makes the outcome contract_violation”
open_points.question: If a succeeded result is both oversized and mismatched, which condition is checked first, and which detail/failure fields are recorded?
options: Size first, yielding contract_violation/value_too_large
Comparison first, yielding output_mismatch
Use the first output in contract order whose issue is found
open_points.default_guess: Check oversized value outputs before expected-output comparison and record contract_violation with value_too_large.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case recorded file outputs
open_points.text: “a file by digest, size and media type only as a FileFactsRef”
open_points.question: Does a many-file output produce one FileFactsRef containing all files or one FileFactsRef per file, and what is produced for a one-file output?
options: One FileFactsRef per output port, with its files tuple holding one or many facts
One FileFactsRef per file
One ref for many but a different ref type for one
open_points.default_guess: Produce one FileFactsRef per output port, preserving file order in its files tuple.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case recorded output order
open_points.text: “For passed and output_mismatch the outputs are recorded” without specifying their tuple order
open_points.question: Are recorded output refs ordered by contract output name, contract tuple order, or sandbox result order?
options: Unicode port-name order
Contract outputs tuple order
Sandbox result tuple order
open_points.default_guess: Use contract output tuple order.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case empty-input disclosure
open_points.text: “every output taking [the] highest class of the case's inputs”
open_points.question: What disclosure class is assigned to outputs when the case has no inputs?
options: Open
Reject execution
Delegate the empty tuple to highest_disclosure_class
open_points.default_guess: Delegate the empty tuple to highest_disclosure_class.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case cleanup failure
open_points.text: “When the sandbox reports detail cleanup_failed the execution is recorded crashed…”
open_points.question: Does any SandboxResult with detail_code cleanup_failed override its reported outcome, including succeeded or another failure outcome?
options: Yes, cleanup_failed always forces crashed
Only override when sandbox outcome is crashed
Treat inconsistent combinations as contract_violation
open_points.default_guess: Any cleanup_failed detail forces crashed and then StopRequiredError.

open_points.subject: execute_trial_case StopRequiredError
open_points.text: “then StopRequiredError is raised” but no constructor signature or required payload is given
open_points.question: How must StopRequiredError be instantiated after recording the cleanup failure?
options: No arguments
The failure_detail string
The recorded TrialExecution
open_points.default_guess: Raise StopRequiredError with no arguments.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version identity timing
open_points.text: “contract_version_id is computed right after the purpose rule” but ContractVersionContent requires ResourceBounds, while ResourceBoundsRequest fields may be None and are not validated or converted until the later resource-bound checks
open_points.question: How can ContractVersionContent and its identity be constructed before validating that all requested bounds are positive non-None integers?
options: Validate/convert bounds before identity despite the stated order
Permit constructing ResourceBounds with invalid or None fields solely for identity lookup
Define identity over ResourceBoundsRequest instead
open_points.default_guess: Validate and convert resource bounds before constructing ContractVersionContent, despite the stated identity timing.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version existing slot purpose
open_points.text: “an existing slot whose purpose differs from a given purpose”
open_points.question: For an existing slot, does purpose=None mean ‘do not check/change purpose,’ or does it differ from every string and therefore cause refusal?
options: None means omit the purpose consistency check
None is compared literally and therefore refused
None adopts the stored purpose before identity calculation
open_points.default_guess: Treat None as unspecified and use the existing slot's purpose without refusal.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version port ordering
open_points.text: “ports are taken inputs first then outputs, each by name”
open_points.question: Must the input and output tuples be sorted by Unicode port name before constructing ContractVersionContent, or is sorting only for validation order while original tuple order remains identity-significant?
options: Sort both tuples before validation, identity, storage, and return
Sort only validation traversal and preserve supplied tuple order
Reject tuples not already sorted
open_points.default_guess: Sort each direction by Unicode code point before constructing content and storing it.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version port direction
open_points.text: The function receives separate “inputs” and “outputs” tuples, while every Port also has a direction field, but no check says those values must agree
open_points.question: Must an input tuple port declare direction input and an output tuple port declare direction output, and where does that failure occur in the ordered checks?
options: Validate direction before other per-port checks
Normalize direction from tuple placement
Do not validate direction
open_points.default_guess: Validate direction as a per-port check before disclosure class, though the required refusal order is unspecified.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version schema syntax
open_points.text: “A supported value_schema is a JSON object using only…”
open_points.question: How are invalid JSON, duplicate JSON object keys, noncanonical JSON text, and schemas that are semantically equal but textually different handled for validation and contract identity?
options: Parse strictly but preserve the original text for identity
Parse and canonicalize schema text before identity
Require already-canonical JSON text
open_points.default_guess: Parse as JSON for validation but preserve the supplied value_schema string in the Port and identity.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version schema subset
open_points.text: “properties and required for object … items as one schema for array, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, minimum and maximum”
open_points.question: What types, domains, applicability, and cross-field constraints apply to these keywords—for example nonnegative integer lengths, min <= max, required as unique strings contained in properties, and whether type is mandatory?
options: Apply ordinary JSON Schema semantics for the named keywords
Check only that keywords are allowed and nested schema values recurse
Use a project-specific subset not supplied here
open_points.default_guess: Apply ordinary JSON Schema type requirements, nonnegative integer length bounds, ordered min/max pairs, and object required-name constraints; allow type to be omitted.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version scalar equality
open_points.text: “enum as a non-empty array of distinct scalars, const as one scalar”
open_points.question: What counts as a scalar and as distinct—especially null, booleans versus numbers, and 1 versus 1.0?
options: Use JSON scalar types and JSON semantic equality
Use Python equality
Use canonical JSON byte equality
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical JSON representations to determine distinctness.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version file schema
open_points.text: “a file port's value_schema is the empty object”
open_points.question: Must the schema text be exactly '{}', or may any JSON text that parses to an empty object be accepted and preserved?
options: Accept any JSON representation of an empty object
Require the exact canonical string '{}'
Canonicalize accepted text to '{}'
open_points.default_guess: Accept any text parsing to an empty object and preserve it.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version resource checks
open_points.text: “a resource bound that is None, not a positive integer, or above its release ceiling” names the per-field checks but gives no order among the four fields
open_points.question: In what order are wall_time_ms, memory_bytes, output_bytes, and process_count checked to determine the first refusal?
options: ResourceBoundsRequest field declaration order
Alphabetical field order
Order of the imported ceiling constants
open_points.default_guess: Use ResourceBoundsRequest field declaration order.

open_points.subject: issue_contract_version positive integer
open_points.text: “not a positive integer”
open_points.question: Is bool rejected even though it is a Python int subclass, and are non-built-in integral types accepted?
options: Accept only type(value) is int and value > 0
Use isinstance(value, int), accepting booleans
Accept any numbers.Integral
open_points.default_guess: Require type(value) is int and value > 0, rejecting booleans.

open_points.subject: read operations
open_points.text: “return the stored ContractVersion unchanged,” “return … the latest in store order,” and similar read requirements do not state how by-ID queries behave if multiple records with the same ID are returned
open_points.question: For supposedly unique IDs, should the first, last, or only record be selected, and should duplicates be treated as corruption?
options: Require exactly one record
Use the first in store order
Use the latest in store order
open_points.default_guess: Use the first stored record for content-addressed entities and the latest only where the prompt explicitly requests latest.

open_points.subject: read_corpus
open_points.text: “The corpus of a contract version is its trial cases in store order, read through read_corpus”
open_points.question: Is this merely describing calls by other functions, or does read_corpus itself need an additional validation/read step beyond CorpusOfContractVersion?
options: Use only the CorpusOfContractVersion query
First call read_contract_version, then query the corpus
The wording intended a different imported function
open_points.default_guess: Use the CorpusOfContractVersion query directly and do not separately validate the contract version.

open_points.subject: read_corpus unknown contract
open_points.text: The function has no VALIDATION_ERROR requirement, while CorpusOfContractVersion may be empty for either an unknown contract version or a known version with no cases
open_points.question: Should read_corpus return an empty tuple for an unknown contract_version_id or raise UnknownReferenceError?
options: Return an empty tuple
Raise UnknownReferenceError
Rely on read_records to distinguish or raise
open_points.default_guess: Return the query's empty trial_cases tuple because only known-empty behavior is specified.

open_points.subject: read_slot query assembly
open_points.text: “per contract version in store order its current corpus digest, its implementations in store order each with its verdicts in store order … and serving_activation its latest Activation”
open_points.question: Which query results define ‘store order’ when records have no store_position fields, and are the tuples returned by read_records guaranteed to already be in that order?
options: Trust every RecordSet tuple to be in store order
Issue RecordsByPosition queries after obtaining hidden positions
Sort by timestamps
open_points.default_guess: Trust read_records result tuples to preserve store order.

open_points.subject: roll_back_slot admitted verdict lookup
open_points.text: “when it holds no admitted verdict over the current corpus digest”
open_points.question: If both admitted and refused verdict records exist for the same implementation and corpus digest, does any admitted verdict authorize rollback or does the latest verdict control?
options: Any admitted verdict authorizes rollback
Latest verdict controls
Multiple verdicts are impossible
open_points.default_guess: Any admitted verdict authorizes rollback, matching ‘holds an admitted verdict.’

open_points.subject: submit_implementation existing record
open_points.text: “an equal existing one writes nothing and is read from the store and used unchanged”
open_points.question: If implementation_id resolves to a stored Implementation whose content is not equal to the newly computed ImplementationContent, should it be reused, refused, or treated as store corruption?
options: Assume content_identity collisions cannot occur
Verify equality and refuse on mismatch
Reuse solely by ID
open_points.default_guess: Assume collision-free identity and reuse the stored implementation.

open_points.subject: try_implementation case validation
open_points.text: “raise UnknownReferenceError for the first named case that does not exist, then RefusedError naming the first named case that belongs to another contract version or is named twice”
open_points.question: Does ‘then’ require resolving every named ID for existence before checking any ownership or duplication, or should all checks be performed per case in argument order?
options: Two passes: all existence checks, then ownership/duplicates
One pass per case: existence, ownership, duplicate
Resolve all records in one query and use query return order
open_points.default_guess: Use two passes so any unknown named case wins over ownership or duplication failures.

open_points.subject: try_implementation explicit case ordering
open_points.text: “execute the named cases … in corpus order”
open_points.question: For an explicit subset, must the argument order be discarded and the selected cases reordered by their positions in the full corpus?
options: Always reorder the subset by corpus order
Execute in the supplied order
Require the supplied order already matches corpus order
open_points.default_guess: Reorder the selected subset by full-corpus order.
